channel.title: ML Engineering Notes
channel.description: Fictional sample feed for agent-ops demos

item.title: Hybrid retrieval beats pure vector search on enterprise documents
item.description: Combining BM25 with dense embeddings via reciprocal rank fusion improved retrieval hit rate on internal policy documents. The post shares an evaluation setup with abstention questions to catch hallucinations in RAG systems.

item.title: Designing evals for LLM features before shipping
item.description: Teams that wrote evaluation sets before changing prompts caught regressions earlier. Recommended metrics include answer accuracy, citation precision and refusal correctness, tracked per release.

item.title: Structured output makes LLM pipelines easier to test
item.description: Constraining model responses to a JSON schema and validating them with typed models removes a whole class of parsing bugs and makes prompt changes safer to roll out.

item.title: Multi-agent orchestration patterns: planner, worker, reviewer
item.description: An overview of common multi-agent designs. A planner agent splits work, worker agents use tools, and a reviewer agent checks results. The article warns that more agents mean more cost and harder debugging, so start with one agent.

item.title: Fine-tuning small models for classification
item.description: For high-volume email or ticket classification, a small fine-tuned model can match a large model on accuracy at a fraction of the cost, but needs labelled data and monitoring for drift.
